name: Porto-Novo
subtitle: Porto-Novo, capital of Benin: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 264,320 people live in the town of Porto-Novo (counted 2013).
Porto-Novo is the city of three names: Adjatchè for the Yoruba, Hogbonou for the Fon, Goun and Ayizo, and Porto-Novo, the name given by Europeans.
The name Porto-Novo was given in 1730 because of a resemblance to the city of Porto.

parts.text: Porto-Novo is the city of three names: Adjatchè for the Yoruba, Hogbonou for the Fon, Goun and Ayizo, and Porto-Novo, the name given by Europeans.
The name Porto-Novo was given in 1730 because of a resemblance to the city of Porto.
Hogbonu was founded in the 16th century by Aja princes who left Allada after Allada was taken by the kingdom of Abomey.
Porto-Novo lies in south-east Benin, 30 km from Cotonou and 12 km from the Nigerian border.
Goun and Yoruba people make up more than 80 per cent of the population, alongside Aja, Toffin, Mina and other groups.
Porto-Novo is one of the three communes with a special status in Benin.
Its status as capital was confirmed after independence in 1960, and the National Assembly sits in the Governors' Palace where independence was proclaimed.
In 2009 the city counted 450 Afro-Brazilian buildings; by 2016 fewer than 400 were left.
Porto-Novo was once a great kingdom alongside Abomey.
The city's rhythms such as AkoNhoun, Adjogan and Kaka continue to be performed by groups such as the Ballet de la capitale and Ashakata.

parts.text: 264,320 in 2013, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Town (ville) of Porto-Novo, RGPH4 2013 total population, as reproduced in a master thesis table of the successive censuses (1961: 64,000; 1979: 133,168; 1992: 179,138; 2002: 223,552); the INSAE/INStaD primary pages returned HTTP 503 and could not be read.

items.text: Hogbonu was founded by Aja princes from Allada.
The city was baptised Porto-Novo because of its resemblance to Porto.
King Soji signed a first protectorate treaty with the French.
A second treaty with King Toffa I marked the installation of the French colonial administration.
The French created the colony of Dahomey, of which Porto-Novo became the capital.
Benin's first museum was created by IFAN in 1943 to popularise the history of the kings of Danhomè (the Abomey museum).
Porto-Novo kept its capital status after the independence of Benin in 1960.
The Alexandre Sènou Adandé Ethnographic Museum was created by the IRAD in 1966, according to this account.
The Musée Honmè was created in 1988 in the palace of the former kings of Hogbonou.
The 2013 census (RGPH4) counted 264,320 inhabitants in the town of Porto-Novo.
